# Bounded completion arrays: public Kafka comparison

Predeclared for #3083 candidate `46b04e8d955c3dc178c0cb0524a2d3b55dfaddad`, containing main `551d4d0825dca64b7143d6f18fc2b13baaf1fe0a` as both controls. This candidate caps runtime completion owners at 1,024 slots. More owners can add amortized per-chunk costs; reduced initial array reservation does not waive CPU, throughput, latency or allocation requirements.

Run `dispatch-loaded-adjacent`: all four existing public Kafka modes, with A1/B/A2 adjacent for each mode on one ubuntu-latest VM. Build both exact products and validate every mode on both before measuring. Each fresh measured process receives 361 seconds offered warmup (at least 360 completed) and 180 seconds measured workload. Keep the same rates, fixture, broker resets, tiered runtime, affinity and recorder as `ADJACENT-FULL-EXPERIMENT.md`. Preserve every maximum, histogram, time series, JIT event, completion count, commit, backlog and exact binary/source hash. Criteria remain 3% completed throughput/CPU, 5% actual-message p50/p99/max and at most 1 B/message allocation increase against each control. Missing precision, material drift and startup transitions remain INCONCLUSIVE.

Prior run 34318593774 failed before measurement at compilation of the private dispatcher fixture. Its predecessor B was `db184957ce6534e4c6b0dd075c5ebe5fa3a816f8`; it provides no timed comparison. Local API adaptation then exposed another mismatch: the inherited #3117 zero-allocation assertion applies to optimized key dispatch, while the existing dispatcher on main allocates 928 B/record and this candidate 880 B/record in the repeated-key smoke diagnostic. This does not constitute completion-path zero-allocation evidence. The private assertion remains intact, and this run explicitly measures only the public Kafka scope. It cannot certify sparse/reverse completion, private dispatcher microbenchmarks or focused shutdown; those remain separate requirements.

The immediately preceding valid pending-batch pilot 34311913277 measured B `db184957ce6534e4c6b0dd075c5ebe5fa3a816f8` at 121/120 seconds. A1/B/A2 CPU was 58614.517/57771.075/59759.975 ns/message (-1.44%/-3.33%, control +1.95%). Maxima were 15.597/15.338/9.259 ms (+65.66% versus A2, controls -40.64%), with JIT/worker transitions. It was INCONCLUSIVE. The older differently pinned/hardware run 34294127203 had +3.48%/+3.50% pending-batch CPU losses; that cross-run difference was not causally attributed to the product. No full accepted loaded baseline exists.

This is a new causal candidate and explicitly bounded experiment, not an unchanged repeat of the failed full matrix. It retains both controls and all public Kafka modes. It does not waive missing coverage, the unresolved local Windows/TUnit allocation failure, or the repository's repeat limits. Successful execution never sets the performance gate to PASS.
